newsitem.title: USA: Texas spot power dives on mild weather, lower gas.
newsitem.headline: Texas spot power dives on mild weather, lower gas.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) dove Friday, extending Thursday's loss on milder temperatures and lower swing natural gas prices in the cash market.
"The mild weather has been driving it lower," said a Houston marketer.

Saturday in-state temperatures were predicted to peak in 60s-70s Fahrenheit degrees and bottom in the 20s-40s, up 10-20 degrees from today's levels. Temperatures in Texas expected to warm to 10 degrees above normal Sunday and Monday.
Extended outlook showed a cool front would move into the region middle of next week but much less severe than the system that froze much of the Midwest this week.
"We don't know bad it's going to be yet," said another ERCOT marketer.
Swing gas in south Texas slipped to $4.20 per million British thermal unit (mmBtu) area from Thursday's $4.60.
On the New York Mercantile Exchange, January Henry Hub gas futures were last up 2.1 cents at $4.430/MMBtu after erasing an early 13.9 cent loss.
ERCOT firm, peak power for a 16-hour block for Monday delivery collapsed to $30.00-$35.00 a megawtt hour, down more than $15.00 from Thursday's $45.00-$47.00 for Friday.
Monday's ERCOT peak, firm power halved Wednesday's day-ahead prices.
Firm off-peak ERCOT deliveries for Monday were thinly talked in $20.00-$25.00 range, down from Thursday's $25.50-$26.50.
Non-firm deliveries for Monday were in line with firm prices, market sources said.
ERCOT power for the rest of December thinly discussed at $25.50-$26.50, off sharply from Thursday's $45.00-$46.00 area.

ERCOT January/February prices were pegged in the $38.50-$40.00 range amid a rebound in natural gas futures in afternoon trading. Today's quote compared with $35.00-$39.00 Thursday. March ERCOT power was discussed at $29.00-$31.00.
